To address these limitations, we introduce ShiftRAG, a decoupled RAG framework that employs a single LLM backbone but isolates discriminative retrieval learning from autoregressive generation.…

items.title: Answer Correction with Verifiable Rewards: A Gemma-Family Study of Multi-View Driving QA
items.summary: Multi-camera driving question answering provides a discrete test of vision-language models, but post-training gains can reflect changed selected answers or improved answer extraction. We investigate this distinction within the Gemma model family using archived, task-linked WaymoQA evaluations. A zero-shot diagnostic on 5,519 test questions spans effective-small, mixture-of-experts, unified, and dense checkpoints, with serving differences disclosed rather than interpreted as architecture effects. The strongest controlled evidence is a matched-harness Gemma-4-12B base/GRPO pair: accuracy rises from 73.78% to 75.43%, a gain of 1.65 percentage points with a scene-cluster bootstrap interval of [+0.84, +2.41]. There are 215 improvements and 124 regressions; 213 improvements start from an extractable but incorrect base answer, and only two recover previously unextractable responses.…

items.title: ROSE: Deep Learning exchange-correlation functional from reduced density-matrix representations
items.summary: We introduce ROSE, a deep-learning exchange--correlation energy functional built from the occupied-state density matrix. On GMTKN55 and on additional external benchmarks considered in this work, ROSE improves over modern neural network functionals trained under matched protocols and is on average more accurate than, or on par with, most hybrid and range-separated hybrid functionals considered here. On the experimental benchmarks considered here it has leading accuracy across hybrids, range separated hybrids, and neural functionals. These results motivate nonlocal density-matrix representations as a route to systematic improvement of learned XC functionals with low computational cost.

items.title: Canonic hemoglobin-oxygen equilibrium: Reassessing the role of cooperativity
items.summary: Hemoglobin-oxygen equilibrium is normally studied within the grand canonical ensemble, which assumes that each hemoglobin is immersed in a reservoir of unbound oxygen molecules of the plasma. We show that this assumption is incorrect inside the RBC (red blood cell or erythrocyte), where the hemoglobin concentration is larger than the concentration of unbound oxygen in plasma. We suggest a better model, where a single hemoglobin and a few oxygen molecules around it reach a canonical equilibrium at a fixed volume (determined from the RBC structure) and a fixed temperature. The basic models of hemoglobin-oxygen equilibrium -- Pauling's model and Monod-Wyman-Changeux model -- can be reformulated for this canonical situation. They predict cooperative interaction energies, which are significantly lower than predictions of the same models in the grand canonical ensemble.…

items.title: AdKnob: Ad Intensity Control and Labeling for LLM-Native Advertising
items.summary: Large language model (LLM)-native advertising has emerged as a viable monetization channel as LLM service providers seek sustainable revenue streams. However, integrating native ads into LLM responses introduces two largely understudied challenges: (1) controlling ad intensity -- how prominently advertising content appears -- and (2) ad labeling -- identifying which segments of the generated text constitute advertising. We propose AdKnob, a framework jointly addressing both challenges. For ad intensity control, we introduce new ad control tokens without pretrained semantic associations and align the model via direct preference optimization to generate ads at each desired level. For ad labeling, we propose an attention rollout-based attribution mechanism that identifies ad segments by tracing their attribution to input ad-related tokens, requiring no additional inference cost.…

items.title: AI Data Analysis: A New Approach - Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis
items.summary: AI data analysis today is three fragmented worlds: LLMs understand semantics but cannot compute; BI aggregates precisely but is stateless; ML processes large-scale data on a stateful kernel but lacks semantics. This paper proposes a combination mechanism, named Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis, that fills a still-open gap - the multi-engine joint context: the data context is embedded into LLM conversational analysis, where the LLM serves only as the semantic, reasoning, and orchestration layer (not computation) and connects four engines through the 1M context window - Python and R ML kernels, SQL over relational databases, Cypher over graph databases - yielding two multiplications, "semantics and precise computation" and "relational and graph", under enterprise-grade governance.…

items.title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework for Autonomous Topology Optimization
items.summary: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging.…

items.title: PhoneValue-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark and Datasets for Consumer Smartphone Recommerce Valuation
items.summary: As consumer smartphone recommerce scales, buyers must quote binding repurchase prices from seller-uploaded multi-view photos and diagnostic screenshots before devices reach the warehouse. Accurate remote valuation requires fusing noisy cosmetic evidence with identity, battery, lock, and channel risk from screenshots and staff forms, since an error in any modality changes both grade and payout. However, existing multimodal resources mainly target general VLM competence, screen reading, or factory defect detection, and largely overlook staff-aligned trade-in fields, dual appearance/staff ground truth, and executable valuation scorecards.…

items.title: CheXPoT: Post-Hoc Visual Verification and Correction of VLM-Generated Radiology Reports
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promise for chest radiograph report generation, but adoption remains limited because of hallucinated findings that are not grounded in the image. Correcting these hallucinations and improving overall report quality remains a significant challenge. Prior work has addressed this problem by refining models with reinforcement learning, preference optimization, or chain-of-thought supervision, often at substantial compute cost. To address this gap, we introduce CheXPoT, a program-of-thought (PoT) framework that verifies each generated finding against image features and removes those it cannot ground. CheXPoT decomposes generated reports into predicates with RadGraph and an LLM, grounds these predicates against a DenseNet-121 and Grad-CAM visual evidence table, executes PoT verification code, and rewrites reports after removing unsupported predicates.…

items.title: Informative Fisher Modes in Neural Networks as a Result of Explicit Symmetry Breaking
items.summary: Learning in a neural network takes place on a high dimensional, non-convex loss landscape, the Hessian curvature of which dictates the learning dynamics. Despite its high dimensionality, the large number of architectural symmetries explains some of the geometric of this landscape, in particular flat directions, i.e. near-zero modes of the Hessian. These architectural symmetries have therefore been suggested as an organizing principle of deep learning. It remains an open question, though, wether there are additional organizing principles in the remaining degrees of freedom in the learning dynamic. Here we identify task-dependent contingent symmetries as such an additional organizing principle. We show that non-flat learning directions emerge due to explicit breaking of these contingent symmetries. We isolate this symmetry in an analytically solvable minimal model.…

items.title: Beyond Synthesis Conditions: Linking In-situ Growth Dynamics to Carbon Nanotube Forest Properties through Multimodal Machine Learning
items.summary: Machine learning for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) has largely mapped static synthesis conditions to final properties, implicitly treating these conditions as a complete description of growth. Here, we test this assumption by integrating gas-flow conditions with in-situ time-resolve growth profiles (growth curves) of vertically aligned CNT forests. We introduce an observation-window analysis, in which prediction is evaluated as a function of observation time by providing models with the growth curve only up to progressively later times, to determine not only whether a property can be predicted, but when the necessary information becomes available during synthesis. Clustering of normalized growth curves revealed distinct growth patterns independent of final forest height.…

items.title: Architecting Fairness-Aware LLM Interactions
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as decision-support tools but may generate stereotypical, discriminatory, or unfair responses. As LLMs become embedded in decision-critical software systems, fairness can no longer be treated as a downstream evaluation step, but must become an architectural concern of the interaction itself. Yet current fairness approaches operate as standalone evaluation techniques, lacking a reusable mechanism to verify and mitigate violations at runtime. We propose a fairness-assurance architecture grounded in three reusable design patterns, instantiated as a multi-agent framework that evaluates and iteratively refines LLM responses before delivery.…

items.title: STEER: Route-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Vision-language action (VLA) models excel for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet their tendency to over-invoke chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning mirrors a human cognitive pitfall: overthinking. Just as deliberate reasoning can slow or mislead human judgment in routine tasks, excessive CoT in VLA incurs unnecessary compute overhead and can paradoxically degrade planning performance. Recent research tackles this via adaptive reasoning, which dynamically modulates inference complexity by selectively triggering CoT for complex scenes while responding directly to routine ones.…

items.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
items.summary: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR).…

items.title: Optimal portfolio and consumption under no-shorting constraints: The exploratory formulation and reinforcement learning
items.summary: We develop a reinforcement-learning framework for the continuous-time optimal portfolio-consumption via utility maximization under no-shorting portfolio constraints. We adopt the exploratory formulation under entropy regularization and impose no-shorting constraint through a componentwise nonnegative conditional-mean constraint on the class of admissible randomized policies, while the sampled actions are allowed to be negative during the training. For CRRA utility, we derive the homothetic value function and the optimal Gaussian portfolio and Gibbs consumption policies under some model conditions and establish a verification theorem. These results allow compatible parameterizations in actor, critic, and $q$ functions for a constrained policy-iteration algorithm.…

items.title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget.…

items.title: glincker/awesome-selfhosted-ai
items.summary: Curated list of self-hosted open-source AI: local LLMs, chat UIs, agents, MCP servers, RAG, speech and image generation. Health-checked weekly, dead projects removed automatically.

items.title: Aevonix/FlashAlign
items.summary: ReAlign models instantly, on demand. Per-request alignment for verified users and channels, or Always On. Use directly or with Hermes, OpenClaw and custom harnesses.

items.title: PREM: Prediction-Regulated Memory for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: A robot's next action can depend on recent motion or earlier visual evidence absent from its current observation. A recurrent visual-memory architecture can retain this history in a visual state, but its usefulness depends on what the state represents and how it is updated with new observations. We introduce Prediction-Regulated Memory (PREM), a framework that uses action-conditioned future prediction to guide both memory learning and updating in vision-language-action policies. During training, predicting future visual features provides temporal supervision for memory learning. During execution, PREM compares current visual features with the prediction made at the preceding decision and uses the spatially normalized prediction discrepancy to regulate updates to the visual state at each spatial location.…

items.title: AgentPRO: Coordinating Compiler Optimizations for LLM Agent Workflows
items.summary: LLM agents repeatedly return to a model to generate actions and interpret tool results, incurring repeated context processing and generation overhead. Yet a value needed to execute an action need not be observed by the model to generate that action. This distinction creates an optimization opportunity: reconsider where model decisions are necessary, together with the work performed between them. We present AgentPRO, a compiler framework for optimizing agent workflows as execution information becomes available. AgentPRO organizes planned duties, generation regions, and concrete operations in a hierarchical representation, distinguishing execution dependencies from observations required for generation. Region transformations combine compatible duties into fewer model requests, while operation transformations reduce redundant context and tool work.…

items.title: Autonomous Analysis of Thermoelectric Materials Big Data by Multi-Agentic AI and Construction of a Knowledge Base and Specialized AI
items.summary: Extracting knowledge from large databases of experimental materials data requires repeated analyses and reusable records of their choices and results. We developed Multi-Agentic AI (MAA), a multi-agent system in which AI agents with distinct roles analyze experimental thermoelectric data under predefined instructions and quality checks, saving analysis records traceable to their sources. In four experiments varying theme and cycle counts, we measured what accumulated in these records. In the largest experiment (100 analyses across 10 themes and 10 cycles), concept co-occurrences were concentrated within themes, vocabulary was shared across themes and some relation descriptions were first detected in later cycles. A specialized AI that searches this experiment's knowledge bases and reads their analysis records answered materials questions with cited sources.…

items.title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
items.summary: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution.…

items.title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI
items.summary: A central obstacle in realizing color center cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is inhomogeneity, or disorder, among individual emitters. As the number of emitters increases, so does the complexity of the experimental data, making it difficult to quantify the present physical mechanisms of disorder. Here we introduce an artificial intelligence-driven model discovery framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent, equipped with tools and a structured workflow, proposes candidate Hamiltonian and Lindbladian models, generates computational tools, and quantitatively evaluates competing physical hypotheses. We apply the workflow to three previously published experimental cavity-QED datasets collected from color centers in diamond and silicon carbide. Across the experiments, the agent successfully identifies physical models for the system and characterizes the disorder.…

items.title: LM6-CastBench: A Geometry-Aware Simulation Dataset for Transient Thermal Prediction in LM6 Sand Casting
items.summary: Transient thermal fields during solidification connect casting process conditions and cooling behaviour to the formation of defect-prone regions in aluminum cast ings. Repeatedly solving this thermal problem across geometries and process conditions is computationally expensive, motivating data-driven surrogate models. However, existing machine-learning studies on casting thermal behaviour rely on study-specific simulation databases that do not support reproducible geometry-level benchmarking. We introduce LM6-CastBench, an open simulation dataset for geometry-aware learning of transient thermal fields in LM6 aluminum sand casting, combining three geometry families, ten variants per family, five pouring tempera tures, and three mould temperatures (450 geometry-process cases in total).…

items.title: Learning from an Imitable Teacher: Competition Solution for the MetaFine Challenge
items.summary: The MetaFine Open Competition (RoboFineMani workshop, CoRL 2026) evaluates fine-grained manipulation beyond binary success. Its five simulated tasks, from grasping a bottle by an instructed part to inserting letter-shaped pegs with 4 mm clearance, are scored on perception under lighting and camera changes, instruction understanding, and behavior. This report presents Team Friday's solution, which got second place with an overall score of 0.947, more than twice the $π_0$ baseline. Instead of fine-tuning a large vision-language-action (VLA) model, we train one 19M-parameter policy per task with a separate instruction classifier and focus on the data, all generated in the simulator by a privileged scripted teacher, including its corrections of the student's mistakes.…

items.title: ECG2Gene: Deep Learning-Based Germline Tumor Susceptibility Gene Risk Assessment Using Electrocardiograms
items.summary: Electrocardiograms (ECGs) may contain physiological information related to hereditary cancer susceptibility, but its relationship with future cancer risk remains unclear. Here, we present ECG2Gene, a two-stage deep-learning framework that derives digital phenotypes related to germline tumor susceptibility from routine 12-lead ECGs and predicts future cancer risk. In Stage 1, carrier status for pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in ATM, BRIP1, CHEK2, PALB2, BRCA1, and BRCA2 supervises a multitask model that generates six continuous ECG-derived gene scores. In Stage 2, XGBoost integrates these scores with clinical variables to predict subsequent breast and ovarian cancer in women and prostate cancer in men. We also introduce ECG-Wide Association Analysis (EWAS) to characterize associations between ECG-derived gene scores and ECG waveforms.…

items.title: Words Before Pixels: Selective Modality Routing for Vision-Language Model Unlearning
items.summary: Vision-language model (VLM) unlearning is often treated as an objective-design problem: given multimodal forget data, the goal is to optimize a loss that removes undesirable behavior while preserving retained capabilities. We argue that this view overlooks an equally important data-centric question: how should each forget example be represented before optimization? Existing methods typically keep image-conditioned failures in their original image-text form, implicitly assuming that pixels are the right route for unlearning whenever pixels appear in the input. We challenge this assumption by constructing modality-decomposed versions of VLM benchmarks, enabling controlled comparisons among image-only, text-only, and multimodal representations of the same examples.…

items.title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
items.summary: Conversational text-to-SQL interfaces could give healthcare professionals natural-language access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but evidence for their real-world usability remains limited: prior evaluations have relied largely on curated benchmarks with fully specified questions or on simulated users. We report a user study in which 14 physicians who regularly work with EHR data used both a single-turn and a conversational multi-turn text-to-SQL interface over the MIMIC-IV database in a within-subjects design; dialogue analyses additionally drew on interaction logs from 21 healthcare professionals across the main study and two pilot studies.…

items.title: Implications of the PXP ground-state sign structure for neural-network variational Monte Carlo
items.summary: Positive-definite neural-network quantum states cannot directly represent the ground state of the PXP Hamiltonian, since the ground-state wavefunction carries a nontrivial relative-sign structure. Building on the chiral symmetry of the PXP Hamiltonian, we show that this sign structure is fixed exactly by the parity of the total up-spin number: a diagonal unitary transformation that assigns a sign to each spin configuration according to this parity maps the PXP Hamiltonian to its negative, rendering the transformed Hamiltonian stoquastic on the Rydberg-blockaded Hilbert space. Since the configuration graph of allowed configurations is connected, the Perron-Frobenius theorem guarantees a unique, strictly positive ground state of the transformed Hamiltonian, yielding an exact sign rule for the ground state of the original Hamiltonian in terms of the parity of the up-spin number.…

items.title: Multi-Estimate Elicitation Does Not Uniformly Debias Language Model Judgments
items.summary: Does eliciting five weighted estimates within a single response change how a language model responds to information? Across anchoring, hindsight, base-rate, conjunction, and status-quo/default tasks, we compare direct numerical answers with a multi-estimate response format, contrasting source framings, explicitly random cues, and probability-consistency constraints. We evaluate three completed configurations--gpt-6.1-sol, claude-sonnet-5.5, and Qwen3-8B (reasoning disabled, analyzed descriptively). In the first two configurations, direct elicitation yielded near-zero irrelevant-anchor indices and status-quo effects, while remaining responsive to informative sources and informed advice.…

items.title: Dataset Mismatch Matters in Group Relative Policy Optimization for Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: Recently, reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) is practically very important, where the leading approach is group relative policy optimization (GRPO) that typically faces a trade-off between rollout efficiency and downstream performance. To improve efficiency while preserving performance, existing selective rollout methods mainly exploit only source-side training dynamics to optimize the discrete distribution over source prompts. However, in practice, the source training dataset is rarely identically distributed to the target test dataset. When such a mismatch exists, due to legal or privacy constraints, it is usually not acceptable to share target prompts themselves with the RLVR trainer.…

items.title: Conic Certification of Transformer Attention
items.summary: Attention is the computational core of large language models, yet the verifiers that bound how far an attention head's output can move under input perturbations give no guarantee on how loose their bounds are. A weak certificate therefore cannot be told apart from a fragile model. We develop a conic programming theory of attention certification that supplies this guarantee. We prove that the difficulty lies not in the softmax but in the bilinear interaction of a varying query with the keys. This interaction makes certification NP-hard over boxes and inapproximable once the attention logits can move by a constant amount. A fixed query or listed token substitutions, by contrast, make the exact worst case efficiently computable.…

items.title: SaddleSense: Saddle-Shaped Modules for 3D Shape Sensing with Single-Axis Off-the-Shelf Bend Sensors
items.summary: Accurate posture feedback is essential for precise control of continuum robots. Off-the-shelf bend sensors measure curvature about only one axis; without a suitable mounting arrangement, they can restrict robot motion and provide incomplete posture information. SaddleSense introduces a 3D-printed thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) saddle-shaped lattice that holds one commercial bend sensor along each curved edge. Because each sensor flexes within its own channel rather than spanning the segment axially, the lattice converts multi-axis body deformation into sensor curvature without tying segment length to sensor length. Each four-sensor module accommodates two-axis bending, contraction, and extension while quantifying all three deformation modes across its four readings.…

items.title: Can agents reliably design therapeutic antibodies?
items.summary: Recent work has demonstrated agents driving protein design workflows, either through orchestration of specialized tools or direct manipulation of sequences. Yet the fidelity with which agents follow protein design instructions and the factors contributing to their effectiveness remain understudied. We examine agentic antibody design under two settings: when explicit molecular-editing instructions are provided and when agents receive only previously-scored sequences and are prompted to propose improvements. We call the first task-guided and the second black-box design. For the task-guided setting, we curate ten expert-validated affinity-improvement tasks and show that LLM judges closely reproduce programmatic evaluations of instruction following. We then study two augmentations: access to antibody-relevant tools and to previously scored design history.…

items.title: Distinguishing among reasoning levels of GPT 5.5 Pro via a grammar lens benchmark
items.summary: Does the level of test-time processing effort affect a language model's computational capability? A formal grammar-lens benchmark method, derived from the theory of computation, generates novel data at specified levels, each successively more computationally powerful than the levels below. Using this data, we tested GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.5-Pro-Medium, -High, and -XHigh, showing incrementally increased acceptance of test data: 16, 40, 43, and 52\%, respectively, illustrating the benchmark's ability to discern fine-grained differences among models' added test-time reasoning levels. Additionally, as test-time compute effort increases, model responses diverge from human responses to the same data. This increasing disagreement may turn out to be broadly characteristic of more capable language models, introducing the potential of a general capability-versus-alignment conflict.

items.title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs
items.summary: Reasoning-oriented post-training enables large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks via multi-step inference. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on high-quality reasoning traces is a particularly efficient approach, but its effectiveness depends critically on careful data curation. Existing pipelines rely on a costly generate-then-filter paradigm: large pools of long reasoning traces are produced by multiple teacher models and subsequently filtered for difficulty and diversity using additional LLMs, often requiring weeks of computation. In this work, we propose SFTProbe, a fundamentally different approach that bypasses this pipeline by directly predicting the quality of reasoning data. We show that a brief LoRA-based adaptation, combined with evaluating loss on only 5% of each reasoning trace, suffices to estimate both difficulty and diversity.…

items.title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberatio
items.summary: Deterministic multi-agent LLM deliberation can exactly re- play a fixed transcript, yet exact replay alone does not test local resistance to controlled internal interventions. Because each response becomes context for later agents, a changed greedy token can redirect a transcript-mediated execution. We present a white-box audit of this local failure mode in a five-agent committee under greedy decoding. We prospectively select low- and high-margin token positions, require exact no-op re- play, inject norm-relative residual displacements, and measure first transcript divergence within ten generated tokens. Low- margin positions are more branch-sensitive than high-margin controls, while matched margin-reducing gradient directions branch substantially more often than margin-increasing con- trols.…

items.title: Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents extend their capabilities with skills, each with a name, a description, and a body. Under progressive disclosure, an LLM router selects skills by name and description alone and loads only the selected bodies. Skill libraries grow continually as users and agents add new skills. Because the router relies on this metadata, a similar new skill can displace an earlier one, breaking previously correct routing even though the earlier skill and the router are unchanged. This routing interference is aggravated for public skills, whose descriptions may not match their bodies. We formulate the problem as lifelong skill routing, a class-incremental continual learning problem. A solution must keep earlier skills selectable without suppressing new ones.…

items.title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
items.summary: Borophene, a monolayer of boron, is distinctive among two-dimensional materials owing to its unique properties, including polymorphism and potential applications in quantum technologies and energy conversion and storage. Nevertheless, its applications are hindered by the strong binding of borophene to metal substrates, which impedes the realization of freestanding borophene. Alternative substrates with tunable binding to borophene are therefore highly desirable. Since boride layers arise during borophene synthesis on metals, borides provide potential alternative substrates for borophene synthesis. In this work, we investigate the binding energies and interactions between borophene and 1356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases (v1/6 and v1/9), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML).…

items.title: Reflex: Fast Robot Policy Serving by Reusing and Correcting Past Actions
items.summary: Modern robot policies often perform expensive inference to generate action chunks, making serving a latency bottleneck for real-time control and a throughput bottleneck for multi-robot serving. Building on the success of caching in image, video, and audio generation, recent robot-policy advances have reported promising speedups by reusing intermediate denoising states to avoid redundant computation. Surprisingly, we find that such reuse often offers little advantage over simply running fewer denoising steps from fresh noise, without any cache. Moreover, accelerating denoising leaves the expensive policy backbone intact, which can account for 70% of GPU time. We present Reflex, a serving layer that turns past policy executions into a backbone-free path for future decisions.…

items.title: Behavioral Steering of Vision-Language-Action Models in the Low-Parameter Regime
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to adapt pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs). We investigate the problem of behavioral steering: adapting a VLA's execution style to preferences such as carrying objects higher. To investigate how little trainable capacity such steering requires and how much pretrained capability can be retained, we freeze an OpenVLA-OFT 7B policy and optimize TinyLoRA adapters with 8 to 384 trainable parameters using either policy-gradient RL (GRPO) or evolutionary search (CMA-ES). With just 256 trainable parameters, we raise carry height by 120 mm on trained tasks at 92% success and by 74 mm on a held-out task at 80% success. By rescaling the learned update, we can tune the trade-off between style gains and capability retention without retraining.…

items.title: Agentic Context Management for Multi-Turn Human-AI Conversations
items.summary: LLMs degrade in multi-turn conversation partly because of context pollution: the model's own earlier outputs stay in context and anchor later turns, so an early misreading of the user's intent can persist after the user corrects it. Assistant omission (AO), dropping every assistant message, removes this pollution but fails when interaction is referential: later turns refer back to drafts, decisions, and tool-call results that exist only in assistant turns. We propose Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), a training-free method in which a separate analyzer (1) consolidates the task specification from the user's messages alone, (2) audits the assistant's prior outputs against it, and (3) edits the context, either appending the analysis or discarding the assistant side and rebuilding the context from the specification. A second finding: pollution is contagious.…

items.title: AStockArena: Beyond Returns, Can We Entrust Real Capital to the Decisions of Financial Agents?
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in dynamic financial trading, yet real-time trading benchmarks mainly evaluate agents by cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance. Such outcome metrics cannot show whether trades are faithfully reported, supported by available evidence, and consistent with account states. We introduce AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for continuous trading in China's A-share market. Under shared market conditions and execution constraints, we evaluate 13 open- and closed-source models over 3,198 sequential decisions.…

items.title: Do Social Influence Pressures Move LLM Agents? Evidence from Delegated Audit Judgment
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly being integrated into complex professional workflows such as auditing and entrusted with judgments under human review. Human auditors are known to yield to social influence pressures from superiors, peers and clients, and this paper asks whether LLM agents yield to the same pressures and, if so, how they respond. In an experiment on twelve model settings, an LLM agent acting as a senior associate in audit analytical review forms an estimate and is then challenged without new evidence by colleagues inside the firm, by a reviewer from another firm and by the client's CFO, with and without a career inducement. Experimental findings show that LLM agents yield to pressure from the engagement partner, from peers and from a reviewer from another firm, but in most settings not to pressure from the client's CFO.…

items.title: Robustness Starts with the Objective: Designing and Certifying Robust LLM-Generated Heuristics
items.summary: LLMs are increasingly used to design heuristics for computer systems. However, most synthesis frameworks evaluate candidates by their average performance, which can mask severe regressions on specific workloads. Even adding adversarial training inputs doesn't eliminate these regressions, and percentile objectives (e.g., optimizing for the 95th percentile) overlook how severe regressions can be beyond the selected threshold. We present TAILOR, a framework that guides LLM synthesis using the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of the cost difference between each candidate and an existing baseline on the same workload. This paired CVaR measures the average difference over the worst fraction of workloads. We show that a negative paired CVaR guarantees improvements in both average performance and tail optimality gap relative to the unknown optimum, without ever computing that optimum.…

items.title: Where Does EEG Help Wearable Freezing of Gait Detection?
items.summary: Freezing of gait (FoG) detectors built on inertial measurement units (IMUs) are accurate while the legs move, but they become unreliable when the legs are nearly still, which is exactly when akinetic freezing, voluntary stopping, and standing must be told apart. Electroencephalography (EEG) captures motor-planning activity that leg sensors cannot, but EEG is impractical for daily use. We ask where EEG helps: as an input at inference time, or only during pretraining, so that the deployed detector still needs only IMUs. We assemble a pretraining corpus of synchronized EEG and IMU recordings (5 datasets, 184 people, 94 hours) and compare six settings that differ only in the modalities used for pretraining and as model input, each with tuned hyperparameters and five independent pretraining runs.…

items.title: Spotting the Artificial: Dialogic Humor Improvisation in Humans and LLMs
items.summary: We propose a methodology for investigating the differences between natural and synthetic language in a challenging setting: humorous improvisational dialogue. Our experimental setting compares human-produced comedy improvisations with the dialogues generated by LLMs in a multi-agent environment that we designed. The analysis combines automated linguistic measures with manual annotation grounded in Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL). The results show that, although LLMs can create coherent and creative scenes, they often fail to reproduce key characteristics of spontaneous spoken interaction. In addition, LLM-generated interactions display a strong tendency toward politeness and positive evaluations, contrasting with the broader range of attitudes found in human humorous improvisation.…

items.title: Where Causal Discovery Breaks on Real Data: Measuring the Assumptions One Property at a Time
items.summary: Causal discovery is usually evaluated on simulators or on systems whose ground truth follows from physics or design. When it fails on other real data, the failure is attributed to assumptions that may not hold, but which ones fail, and by how much, is rarely measured. We measure the observable properties of the data they bear on, one property at a time, on a real panel. The case study follows 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters, with 71 types of corporate action from SEC 8-K filings, 11 financial-statement items, and an expert graph over 651 action-state pairs. The panel breaks measurable requirements of discovery: tails that survive winsorisation, balance-sheet items and revenue close to random walks, and interventions too rare to detect effects of a tenth of a standard deviation in 40 of 71 actions.…

items.title: Psychedelics restructure information in the human brain
items.summary: How do psychedelic drugs alter human brain function? Answering this question relies on our ability to understand how information is stored, transferred, and transformed across the cortex. Here, we leverage a precise mathematical framework for multivariate information decomposition to construct the first comprehensive picture of these processes across five compounds: LSD, psilocybin, ketamine, DMT and 5-MeO-DMT (N=80). We provide a formal and empirical explanation of major prior results, revealing sets of competing underlying phenomena masked by extant approaches. We extend this analysis to novel higher-order phenomena, and we demonstrate how all of these observations can emerge from a minimal generative model in which neural populations operate with reduced self-coupling.…

items.title: Biologically grounded locality priors close the data gap for vision transformers in neural prediction
items.summary: For datasets with thousands of neurons and images, vision transformers have proven successful at predicting neural responses to stimuli. However, they are expected to underperform in low-data regimes, where CNNs and Gaussian processes are considered more effective. We ask whether transformers can be made competitive for small-scale neural prediction, and show that underperformance in this regime can be overturned with the right inductive bias. We equip a vision transformer with a differentiable per-neuron circular crop in feature space. The crop is centered on each neuron's receptive field, with a radius selected per neuron, so the model only sees the small image region that drives that neuron instead of the whole image. This makes the cost of attention scale with the size of the receptive field rather than with the size of the image.…

items.title: Structural Evolution of Neural Networks during Zebrafish Early Development
items.summary: The spatial architecture of neural networks underpins nervous system function, yet dynamic in vivo evidence for their early establishment process remains scarce. Here, using long-term confocal live-cell imaging of transgenic zebrafish, we dissected neural network development across the brain, yolk sac, and spinal cord at single-cell resolution. We reveal that repeated growth cone bifurcation is the fundamental cellular mechanism for network node formation. Despite distinct developmental origins, networks in all three regions exhibit highly conserved dynamics, strictly following Strahler hierarchical ordering and Hack's power-law scaling. Quantitative topological analysis shows that as development progresses, node numbers and clustering coefficients increase, while network density decreases.…

items.title: Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks for Continuous Motor Control: A Biologically Plausible Model of Motor Cortex
items.summary: Motor cortex acquires skilled movements through recurrent spiking dynamics and experience-dependent synaptic plasticity, yet how such circuits learn continuous motor control using biologically local signals remains unclear. Here, we develop a recurrent spiking neural network model of motor cortex that addresses both the computational and biological requirements of motor learning. We first analytically derived the recurrent firing-rate state directly from synaptic input and trained the network by implicit differentiation, thereby avoiding backpropagation through long spike trajectories. We then introduced State-Carry Initialization, which enables closed-loop motor control by continuously carrying the ongoing recurrent state across successive actions.…

items.title: DCAF: Unifying Data Validity, Evaluation Validity and Predictive Modeling for Single-cell Perturbation Simulation
items.summary: Single-cell perturbation profiling is limited by cost and throughput, while computational methods remain constrained by inconsistent evaluation and underperformance relative to simple baselines. Here we present DCAF, a unified framework for single-cell perturbation simulation that that jointly addresses data validity, evaluation validity and predictive modeling. Among its three components, DCAF-data addresses the single-measurement limitation by reconstructing pre- and post-perturbation status using entropy-regularized optimal transport, and is demonstrated on both cell line and multi-cell type datasets. DCAF-criterion evaluates log fold changes in non-silenced genes to improve sensitivity to model error and robustness to zero inflation noise, validated on synthetic datasets. DCAF-model combines JEPA with explicit modeling for regulatory-dynamics modeling for interpretable prediction.…

items.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney
items.summary: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from human kidney tissue. Kidzoi accurately predicts cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility and improves regulatory variant effect prediction in proximal tubule cells by up to 23% in terms of AUROC over existing models.…

items.title: QuantCell: machine learning based cell annotation integrating qualitative and quantitative imaging profiles
items.summary: Recent advances in spatial omics enable high-resolution, multiplexed imaging of RNA and protein expression, but cell annotation remains challenging, particularly in complex tissues with numerous markers or rare cell types. Here, we present QuantCell, a machine learning framework that leverages quantitative imaging data to improve annotation derived from qualitative profiles. QuantCell evaluates multiple models and applies a user-defined false discovery rate to ensure high-confidence annotation. Using PhenoCycler imaging of mouse bone marrow, QuantCell increased annotated cells from 33.1% to 90.2% at 5% FDR, achieving 96.5% accuracy. QuantCell supports diverse imaging platforms and robustly detects rare cell populations.

items.title: Probing Genomic Foundation Models with Splice-Variant Perturbations
items.summary: As benchmarks saturate, traditional validation methods fail to capture the probabilistic representations of genomic foundation models. This study probes self-supervised generalists (NTv3 650M, Evo2 40B, Genos 10B) alongside task-specific specialists (SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, Borzoi) using a mechanistically focused paradigm centered on expert-curated single-nucleotide substitutions within the splicing regions of the exon-rich OPA1 gene. Extending this analysis across the broader corpus of OPA1 mutations, variants of uncertain significance (VUS), and an independent 65-gene dataset of spliceogenic mutations demonstrates that foundation models not only match task-specific networks, but also generalize across mutation types. Training data scale, genetic diversity, and evolutionary context are key for capturing RNA splicing syntax, whereas sparse routing may constrain performance.…

items.title: Small molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra with generative and reasoning models
items.summary: Elucidating the structures of unknown small molecules remains a major challenge in chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery. While nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is the gold standard for structure elucidation, interpreting spectra remains labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge to navigate the vast space of possible structures. Here, we present an AI system for rapid, automated de novo structure elucidation that combines a molecular generative model with a scientific reasoning agent. Its generative component, ChefNMR2, is an atomic flow-matching model that predicts small-molecule structures from molecular formulae and one-dimensional 1H and 13C NMR spectra. ChefNMR2-Agent augments our generative model with large language models (LLMs) to reason over and refine candidate structures.…

items.title: EMBER: Contextualized gene representations enable compositional prediction across cellular perturbations
items.summary: Predicting the effects of individual and combined perturbations is central to identifying context-specific vulnerabilities and designing targeted interventions. Yet learning gene representations that integrate functional relationships with cellular state and transfer across perturbation tasks remains challenging. Here, we present EMBER, a gene-centric foundation model that learns context-dependent functional representations of genes. EMBER combines interaction-guided contrastive learning with masked expression reconstruction during pretraining on a single-cell corpus curated for diversity and balanced sampling across cell types and experimental batches.…

items.title: Single-cell foundation models transfer across deep evolutionary distances
items.summary: Single-cell foundation models are trained mostly on human and other vertebrate cells, yet are proposed as general-purpose models. Whether they transfer far beyond their training species is unknown. We evaluated zero-shot embeddings from Geneformer, scGPT and UCE against PCA and scVI in developmental atlases of Dictyostelium discoideum and Caenorhabditis elegans, separated from humans by 1.2 billion and 600 million years. Without retraining, the models recovered developmental order and preserved organism-specific cell identities. UCE encodes genes by protein sequence and could use 97% of measured genes, whereas Geneformer and scGPT, after ortholog mapping, used under one-fifth. UCE performed most consistently, often exceeding species-native baselines. Restricted to ortholog-mappable genes, it still scored above vocabulary-based models on five of six annotation tasks, some narrowly.…

items.title: Bioactivity foundation model for hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization from sequence data
items.summary: Learning from large-scale bioactivity archives is complicated by heterogeneous assay readouts and differences in data reliability. Here we show that a model that predicts probability distributions over binding affinities from sequence data opens model training to vast and diverse troves of heterogeneous bioactivity data. We develop PSICHIC+, a bioactivity foundation model trained on approximately 82 million protein-ligand records using a distributional objective that preserves quantitative resolution while incorporating variation in data reliability. Given a protein sequence and ligand SMILES, PSICHIC+ predicts binding affinity in milliseconds. In zero-shot virtual-screening benchmarks without target-specific training data, it improves enrichment over regression- and classification-based approaches and performs competitively with leading structure-based methods.…

items.title: Estimating glioblastoma migration-to-proliferation ratio from single time-point MRI data via radial density distribution
items.summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) tumors with a high migration-to-proliferation ratio (D/k) are associated with treatment resistance, motivating the estimation of D/k from routine pre-treatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data and the investigation of mechanisms underlying its heterogeneity across patients. Unlike previous approaches based on nested spherical approximations of enhancing and non-enhancing tumor volumes, we incorporate the spatial arrangement of the enhancing and non-enhancing tumor regions by deriving a 1D tumor density distribution from their segmentations and fitting a 1D reaction-diffusion model to estimate D/k. We achieved an error of under 5% when comparing our method to synthetic density distributions and found excellent correlation with synthetic tumor segmentations (Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) = 0.996).…

items.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
items.summary: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis-regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we quantify the frequency with which pairs of positions are simultaneously accessible on individual molecules. Then, we train ChAI-Net, a neural network that predicts these locus-specific chromatin co-accessibility maps from the underlying DNA sequence.…

items.title: Multi-scale haplotype signatures distinguish among evolutionary processes
items.summary: Natural selection embeds distinct genomic signatures as populations adapt to environmental pressures. Machine learning approaches, particularly deep neural networks, have emerged as powerful tools to detect adaptive signatures from genomic data. While machine learning has dramatically improved our ability to extract these signals from sequence variation, distinguishing among multiple evolutionary processes remains challenging. We introduce SHADES, a deep learning framework that employs information about sequence differences and their frequencies at various spatial resolutions to capture evolutionary signatures at different genomic scales. We found that SHADES has the capacity to distinguish among neutrality, selective sweeps, balancing selection, and adaptive introgression and outperformed several contemporary methods evaluated for both classification accuracy and power.…

items.title: Machine Learning Based Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease using Full Blood Count from a Ghanaian Hospital Population with an Integrated Web Application
items.summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is usually silent until advanced, and the tests confirming it are frequently unaffordable in sub-Saharan Africa, whereas the full blood count (FBC) is inexpensive and widely performed. We assessed whether machine learning applied to the FBC can detect CKD, and how far its reported performance depends on where synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) is applied. Records of 155 patients at the Ho Technical University Hospital, Ghana, 43 (27.7%) with CKD, yielded ten features: age, cardiovascular disease and eight raw FBC parameters. Eleven algorithms, six resampling strategies and thirteen ensembles were compared under repeated stratified cross-validation.…

items.title: Who Publishes During Residency? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Peer-Reviewed Publication Among Residents in the United States
items.summary: Background/Objectives: The Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education requires US residents to participate in scholarship, but no review has pooled how many physician residents publish during training. We estimated the proportion who published at least 1 peer-reviewed article during residency and compared specialties. Methods: In October 2026, we searched PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, ERIC, and ClinicalTrials.gov (protocol, osf.io/eupxr). AI agents screened records, two AI models from different developers independently extracted outcome data, and an author decided every disagreement against the source. Proportions were pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models. Results: Of 172 included studies, 32 US studies (13,450 residents) reported the primary outcome. The pooled proportion was 59.6% (95% CI, 48.7% to 69.6%).…

items.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
items.summary: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. WF uses chunk-wise causal attention to access earlier, cleaner chunks before their denoising is complete, and distributes staggered denoising and cache-refresh stages across full-model replicas to achieve 1F1C: one output chunk per concurrent forward round after pipeline fill.…
items.tldr: Wave Forcing enables efficient continuous long-video generation with consistent appearance and natural motion through co-designed generation, training, and execution, achieving high throughput and quality.

items.title: Words Caught in the Heart: Simulating Person-Specific Expression for Self-Opaque Clients in Psychotherapy
items.summary: Psychotherapy clients may experience distress before they can coherently describe it, and their expression changes with emotion, perceived safety, and trust. Large language model-based client simulators often rely on clinically organized case descriptions, which can encourage responses explaining the client's difficulties more clearly than their current understanding warrants. We propose Pandora, a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models how psychological experience becomes situated, individual expression. Pandora updates psychological and relational states in response to therapist interventions, constructs subjective appraisals and attributions, and plans response content and strategy. A separate expression planner combines these decisions with language patterns distilled from the client's utterances to guide linguistic realization.…
items.tldr: Pandora is a psychotherapy client simulation framework that models evolving psychological and relational states to generate more authentic, individually aligned expressions and reduce AI-like responses.

items.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
items.summary: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video dataset purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling. GameVerse contains 69.7K clips spanning 1,655 hours and 349.6 million frames across diverse first- and third-person gameplay, including 1,358 hours of continuous two-minute sequences, an order of magnitude longer than prior datasets.…
items.tldr: GameVerse is a large-scale gameplay dataset with minute-long sequences and event-aligned annotations that improves long-horizon interactive world modeling.

items.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
items.summary: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. When the commentator sees something it cannot name, it sends the current frames, and the research agent returns a few wiki entries two seconds later while the stream continues. We train only the commentator, on a single game, in two stages.…
items.tldr: StreamDuo pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that retrieves game wiki entries to improve cross-game streaming commentary without training on target games.

items.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
items.summary: Benchmark compression reduces the often prohibitive time and cost of model evaluation by evaluating models on a small benchmark subset that closely matches full-benchmark results. To quantify estimation error, we derive an accurate analytical approximation to the error distribution when estimating full-benchmark scores from a subset, showing that most subsets yield small errors, while a few produce much larger errors, resulting in a long-tailed distribution. This means random sampling alone can achieve surprisingly strong performance with high probability, but remains unstable due to rare large errors. We further show that this instability is inherent to modern foundation models and persists even as more models are evaluated.…

items.title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions. These benchmarks are also public and widely used online, which may be resulting in LLM memorization. Models may perform better on questions that they have seen before. It is also not evident whether smaller models, which are more locally deployable in HIPAA-compliant hospital settings, have achieved human performance.…

items.title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct observations of contact physics, local geometry, and interaction dynamics, making it a vital source of feedback for contact-rich manipulation. However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions.…

items.title: From Lookups to Lessons: Turning Retrieved Knowledge into Parametric Memory
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) helps large language models (LLMs) answer factual questions beyond their training data, but it adds storage and inference costs. Distilling previously retrieved information into parametric memories enables reuse without online retrieval. However, training the memory to mimic a retriever rewards accurate independent predictions, which do not necessarily improve the final output quality when combined with the LLM's existing predictions. To address this, we introduce ResMem, in which the LLM reads retrieved text offline to generate teacher targets. This design avoids storing massive token representations, unlike existing parametric memory approaches such as MLP Memory, which relies on k-nearest neighbor (kNN) datastores.…

items.title: SpBench: An Agent-Native Framework for Cross-Engine Lakehouse Benchmarking
items.summary: SpBench is an agent-native framework for cross-engine lakehouse benchmarking, in production use for benchmarking Snowpark, Snowpark Connect for Apache Spark, and other execution environments across standardized suites -- such as TPCx-BB and TPC-DI -- and custom benchmarks distilled from production workload patterns. It runs continuously across a broad portfolio of workloads, guiding the performance roadmap and detecting regressions for production-scale data engines. Benchmarking has historically been an expensive investment requiring continuous cross-functional collaboration and domain expertise, making it difficult to obtain actionable performance insights.…

items.title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
items.summary: Learning the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems relies on trajectory-based objectives, which require simulating the learned dynamics during training and backpropagating through the numerical scheme, at a cost that grows with the rollout horizon. We show that trajectory-based objectives degenerate as the rollout horizon increases, hindering gradient-based optimization, and that the numerical scheme biases the learned dynamics by constraining the spectrum of the learned Jacobian to its absolute stability region. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Velocity Matching (VM), a simulation-free objective that relies on piecewise-linear interpolation and stochastic collocation, and approximates the velocity population risk to second order in the sampling step.…

items.title: OmniMechanism Design for Human-AI Collaboration with Impressionable Minds
items.summary: As AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, effectively integrating human expertise with AI outputs is critical for reliable decision-making. A substantial body of theoretical work studies optimal mechanisms for human-AI collaboration (HAC), focusing on when to involve humans and how to combine their expertise with AI predictions. However, these approaches largely overlook a key factor highlighted by empirical evidence: human judgments are impressionable and can vary depending on how AI outputs are presented. For example, when AI systems defer decisions to humans, revealing or withholding the AI prediction can significantly influence human judgments. Moreover, existing work neglects deployment-time variability, where conditions, particularly the cost of eliciting human input, may differ substantially from those observed during training.…

items.title: A Spectral Renormalization-Group View of Learning
items.summary: We study how the layers in deep neural networks (NNs) converge, using Wilsonian Renormalization-Group (RG) ideas to organize the spectral picture. During training, these layers often develop heavy-tailed power-law (PL) spectra, and the strongest checkpoints often appear near the PL exponent $α\approx 2$. This pattern raises a simple question: why should this value mark a well-trained layer? The answer is both statistical and physical. Our statistical hypothesis is that $α=2$ marks the boundary between stable if not optimal learning and overfitting via non-self-averaging. The physical answer is that the same value makes the spectral energy gain scale evenly across logarithmic spectral scales, which is the proposed Wilsonian marginal condition.…

items.title: Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries
items.summary: Attribution graphs, an emerging tool in mechanistic interpretability, use transcoders to decompose language model computations into sparse interpretable features connected by causal edges. However, turning a graph into a safety-relevant insight requires hours of manual analysis by experts. We introduce Circuit Oracle, an off-the-shelf LLM equipped with a multi-agent harness and task-specific authored skills, which answers natural-language questions about a target model by reading the attribution graph through tool calls. We evaluate it on three safety-relevant proxy tasks: detecting spurious features in probe circuits, eliciting hidden knowledge from taboo-finetuned models, and suppression jailbreaking via feature-level interventions. Beyond task scores, the oracle produces pruned subgraphs and context-specific feature explanations that we assess qualitatively. Results are mixed.…

items.title: Hacking or Just Failing? A More Capable LLM Monitor Better Separates Reward Hacking from Honest Failure
items.summary: An agent's visible score can exceed its real progress because it gamed the score or because it simply made mistakes, so a useful reward-hacking monitor must tell the two apart. We built a sandboxed task in which an agent can game a completion score, labelled every episode by replaying it and repairing the final state counterfactually, and ran five pre-registered studies. On 60 episodes from a Llama 3.1 8B agent, small local monitors (Llama 3B and 8B) did not separate exploit attempts from honest failures with the same score gap: prompt changes traded missed exploits for false alarms, and the pre-registered primary monitor reached AUC 0.64.…

items.title: Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data
items.summary: Data flywheels promise continuous improvement via insights from deployment data. Understanding how the deployed model succeeds and fails can steer subsequent data collection towards patching failures and reinforcing successes. However, robot deployments create large volumes of high-dimensional rollout data, which is challenging to understand and confidently ground data collection decisions in. To make deployment data easier to analyze and act on, we propose behavior graphs, which compress policy rollouts into a single interpretable, directed graph. We construct the graphs by learning to identify similar behavior modes across rollouts, connecting the behaviors temporally, and finally linking them to outcomes.…

items.title: OpenMed/GLiNER2.5-ClinicalNER-Disease-Spanish-v1
items.summary: token-classification / openmed

items.title: Transformer-Based Reinforcement Learning for Phase I Dose Allocation
items.summary: Phase I dose-finding trials must learn from sparse toxicity observations while limiting exposure to overly toxic doses. We develop a single reinforcement-learning policy for trials with different numbers of ordered dose levels. Each dose is represented as a token containing its normalized position, accumulated patient count, observed dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), and current-dose indicator. A Transformer encoder summarizes the dose tokens, trial-conditioned cross-attention produces a fixed-dimensional trial representation, and a three-action policy chooses de-escalation, staying, or escalation. The final maximum tolerated dose (MTD) decision is deliberately kept outside the learned policy: after the planned sample size, weighted isotonic regression and a prespecified safety cap select the dose closest to the target toxicity probability.…

items.title: CalVLA: Shaping Native Confidence in Vision-Language-Action Policies with Outcome Supervision
items.summary: Can a vision-language-action (VLA) policy signal likely task failure from its own action probabilities? We introduce CalVLA, which shapes native action-token confidence using successful and failed rollouts and an Action-Confidence Alignment (ACal) squared margin-ranking loss. Low-rank adapters update OpenVLA-7B without an auxiliary failure detector. Observations are paired within tasks at similar normalized elapsed times, not necessarily equivalent physical progress. On a held-out test split from 500 LIBERO-10 configurations, adapted confidence achieves a joint failure-discrimination AUROC of $0.7392\pm0.0480$ over three seeds, averaging scores at 130 and 260 steps. Frozen-policy probes reach 0.6146--0.6436, but superiority over the linear probe is statistically inconclusive. For the same confidence summary, AUROC rises from 0.4485 before adaptation to 0.7327 after adaptation.…

items.title: Emergent Control of Ant Learning Walks in a Mobile Robot
items.summary: Before foraging, desert ants perform learning walks (LWs) to acquire visual memories around their nest. With experience, these walks expand, become straighter, and contain fewer visual scans. We previously proposed a model in which these behaviours emerge from the angular mismatch between path integration (PI) and a mushroom-body-inspired visual compass (VC). Here, we test whether this mechanism can generate learning walks on a physical robot, despite the sensory and motor noise inherent to real-world conditions. We implement the model on a four-wheeled robot equipped with a panoramic camera, an IMU and wheel encoders providing compass and stride information for PI, and test it outdoors using a replicated desert-ant experimental setup. The PI--VC mismatch regulates walking speed, turning, pirouettes, and returns to the nest, while PI provides a teaching signal for visual learning.…

items.title: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks
items.summary: Humans possess a remarkable ability to draw inferences from limited data. While some inferences are made intuitively from past experience, others require online reasoning based on novel information given in context. Here, we formalize these strategies, which we term geometric and algebraic inference, and study their computational tradeoffs in humans and neural networks. The geometric strategy gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect underlying relational structure, making subsequent inference cheap. The algebraic strategy flexibly attends to and reasons over novel relations given in context, but costs additional computation at inference time. We identify opposing signatures of these two strategies in transitive inference, a domain widely studied across species, and characterize the conditions under which each is observed.…

items.title: Dependence-Aware Risk Assessment and Optimal Design of AI-Agent Safeguard Systems
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on safeguards to prevent unauthorized actions while preserving legitimate service. However, existing risk assessments often focus on individual safeguard performance while overlooking dependence among safeguard decisions. This paper develops a dependence-aware framework for risk assessment and optimal design of multi-component AI safeguard systems, jointly selecting configurations and operating policies for sequential layered screening and selective verification. We establish stochastic comparisons of layered-screening error probabilities and invocation costs under lower-orthant ordering. For selective verification, we characterize exactly which policies have error probabilities and review costs that respond monotonically to stronger dependence under supermodular ordering.…

items.title: A geometry-aware framework for electromagnetic fields in GATE 10
items.summary: Objective. An increasing number of medical-physics applications require the modelling of charged-particle transport in electromagnetic (EM) fields. We aim to provide GATE 10 users with a flexible mechanism for defining such fields in Monte Carlo simulations while preserving the native Geant4 particle-transport machinery. Approach. Our framework separates the handling of coordinates from EM field evaluation. Fields are attached to geometry volumes, defined in their local frame, and represented by analytic expressions, field maps, or arbitrary Python functions. They automatically follow the position and orientation of these volumes, including in nested and dynamic geometries. We validated the framework against native Geant4 transport and tested coordinate transformations, nested volumes, and dynamic geometry. We also compared the computational cost of the three field representations.…

items.title: Unlearning by Extrapolating a Shrink-and-Heal Lookahead
items.summary: Unlearning aims to make a large language model behave like one retrained without its forget set. Prevailing likelihood-suppression objectives, however, lack an explicit forgetting target: they continually reward lower forget-set likelihood, making forgetting sensitive to the optimization budget. We address this limitation by estimating the direction toward the oracle without training it. Our key idea is to shrink the fine-tuned model toward its pre-fine-tuning weights and briefly re-learn the retain set, thereby removing the forget-specific contribution; in the linearized regime, this shrink-and-heal lookahead moves the model a fixed fraction of the way to the retrained model, its unique fixed point. Our method, SHIFT, extrapolates the lookahead's per-token changes into distillation targets and iteratively refines them.…

items.title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
items.summary: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive. We check whether numbers, dates, person and organization names, and quoted spans survive each rewrite, using a rule-based checker validated by two AI annotators (precision 0.84-1.00, recall 0.93-0.95; no human annotation). In the October 2026 cycle of a public humanizer leaderboard, all 11 commercial tools changed or dropped at least one of these units in 35-65% of the documents that contained one. Most changes were to quoted spans; counting numbers and names alone, 10 of the 11 tools still altered at least one in 20% or more of the documents. The September 2026 cycle was similar (19-50%). An open 12B humanizer kept at least 97% of numbers and names in fact-dense U.S.…

items.title: SPARK: Self-Correcting Embodied Memory via Physical Re-Observation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have seen growing adoption in embodied settings as language-queryable memories of the environment. However, existing approaches often assume a reliable single-episode knowledge base (KB) or accumulate observations across episodes without correcting prior errors. Such errors can persist through incorrect semantic labels, inaccurate object positions, and inconsistent spatial relationships.
